newsitem.title: UK: Granada says no talks with Saudi prince.
newsitem.headline: Granada says no talks with Saudi prince.

text.p: Britain's Granada Group Plc said on Thursday that there had been no fresh negotiations on hotel deals with Saudi billionaire Price al-Waleed bin Talal.

A report in the Financial Times said that the prince had withdrawn from negotiations to buy a package of Granada's European hotels because of a disagreement over price. But a spokeswoman for media and leisure group Granada denied this.
"The prince bought the George V in Paris but has not made any offers for other hotels," she said.
"He has not bid for other hotels and so has not been involved in negotiations on price."

The prince bought the George V from Granada in December for 104 million stg. The property was one of a portfolio of "Exclusive" up-market hotel properties which Granada acquired as part of last year's 3.9 billion stg takeover of Forte.
Granada put the 17 Exclusives on the market last year and has now sold seven of them and also decided to keep London's Grosvenor House, the largest in the portfolio.
The latest deal was clinched on Wednesday when T.C.C. International (Thailand) Co. Ltd bought the Plaza Athenee Hotel, New York for 42.5 million stg.
The value of the Exclusive hotels sold so far tops 400 million stg, a premium to book value of some 65 million.
Those still on the block include the Hotel Eden in Rome, the Ritz in Madrid, the Hotel des Bergues in Geneva and the Bristol in Warsaw.

Prince al-Waleed, grandson of Saudi Arabia's founder, has built a multi-billion dollar business empire with interests in fields such as construction, real estate, banking, travel, broadcasting and supermarkets.
He is believed to be close to sealing a $560 million deal to buy six hotels in the Princess chain from British conglomerate Lonrho Plc.
